newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FORECAST-Genting '96 net seen up mildly.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Genting '96 net seen up mildly.

text.p: Gaming and hotel companies Genting Bhd and Resorts World Bhd are expected to post modest growth in 1996 net profit, analysts said on Monday.

Business for the year ended December 31, 1996 was hampered by renovations at Genting's mountain-top resort outside Kuala Lumpur, where it operates Malaysia's sole casino, as well as by competition from overseas venues, they said.
Analysts said Genting and Resorts World are expected to release results as early as Tuesday. Company officials declined to immediately disclose the results date.

According to The Estimate Directory of analysts' forecasts, Genting -- the 54 percent owner of Resorts World, which comprises all of Genting's gaming business -- is expected to announce 577.4 million ringgit, or 82.2 cents a share, in net profits for 1996.
The company reported profit of 531.46 million ringgit, or 75.7 cents per share, in 1995.
Analysts see Resorts World posting net income of 615.5 million ringgit or 56.3 cents a share last year, up from 546.20 million or 50.0 cents a share in 1995.
"I expect the gaming division to post about 10 to 15 percent growth from 1995," said an analyst at MBf Northern Securities. "I don't foresee any surprises."
MBf Northern's 1996 net profit estimate for Genting is 601 million ringgit, or 85 cents a share.
The addition of extra casino floor space and hotels should put earnings in 1997 on a better footing, analysts said.

"Overall, earnings will be back on the growth path from fiscal year December 1996 onwards due to its ability to cater to more patronage," said a report on Resorts World issued by Jupiter Securities last quarter.
Said an analyst at another firm: "I think most people are expecting that 1996 is a write-off year because of renovations that weren't completed until the end of the year and a few accidents."
Several buses carrying passengers on their way to or from the mountaintop resort were involved in accidents last year. None was owned by Genting or Resorts World.

While some high-rollers have been lured to other regional gaming havens like Macau or Australia, the analyst said, "Domestic consumption is going to come off. People may curtail spending in terms of traveling."
